title: Finding FB2-REV-FND-000029: the validator's safety-requirement verification rule tests the wrong endpoint of the verifies link, so a correctly directed verification link cannot clear the finding it raises

standards_mappings.rationale: Problem resolution management: a material contradiction becomes a recorded problem, not a silent edit.
The obligation to record rather than to conceal.

revision_history.author: quality_engineer
revision_history.description: Corrected the verifies/validates rule in docs/artifacts/tools/corpus.py to read the link's TARGET endpoint, which is the direction master prompt section 13 declares, and added three self-tests proving both directions: a correctly directed link is not flagged, a requirement with no link is flagged, and a link with the requirement as source does not count as verification. Validator findings fell from 21 to 9; self-tests rose from 11 to 14, all passing. Audited every other endpoint-reading rule and found no further inversion.

evidence: Read from docs/artifacts/tools/corpus.py. The rule computes verified = {l['source_id'] for l in links if l.relation_type in ('verifies', 'validates')} and then raises 'safety requirement has no verifies/validates link' for any safety-domain requirement whose id is absent from that set. The master prompt section 13 defines the relation as 'verification measure -> requirement', and the corpus's own convention follows that: the pre-existing finding FB2-REV-FND-000008 states that 'in the corpus's own convention a test measure is the SOURCE and the requirement is the TARGET, so a well-verified requirement appears as a link TARGET, never as a source'. A correctly directed verifies link therefore places the requirement at the target, and the rule, which reads only the source, still reports it as unverified. This was verified on disk after the five security measures were authored: FB2-VER-TMS-000016..000020 each carry a verifies link to FB2-SAF-SEC-000001..000005 respectively, and each requirement is present as a target and absent as a source. The rule's finding count is therefore unchanged by correct work. The same rule is responsible for the seven 'no verifies/validates link' findings against the FSR records, so 12 of the corpus's 21 standing findings come from this single defect.
impact: The corpus's own headline metric for verification coverage is produced by a rule that cannot distinguish a verified requirement from an unverified one. A safety requirement that is fully verified by twenty measures and one that has none score identically. Because the rule under-reports, it under-reports safely: nothing claims coverage it cannot show. But it also means that closing findings FB2-REV-FND-000008..12 is not achievable by doing the work, and a team following the rule literally - adding links in the reversed direction so the rule fires - would corrupt the graph's documented semantics to satisfy a checker.
root_cause: The rule was written as a quick presence check over whichever endpoint was convenient and was never reconciled with the relation's declared direction in the link schema and the master prompt. The mismatch is invisible until someone authors a correctly directed link and observes that the finding does not clear.
resolution: RESOLVED in the validator, by fixing the rule rather than by deleting it, by relaxing it, or by inverting the graph to suit it. The rule in docs/artifacts/tools/corpus.py read verified = {l['source_id'] for l in links if l.relation_type in ('verifies','validates')} and then asked whether each safety requirement's id was in that set. The source endpoint of a verifies link is the MEASURE, not the requirement, so the set could never contain a requirement and the rule reported a gap for every safety requirement including those verified by twenty measures. It now reads verified = {l['target_id'] for l in links if l.relation_type in ('verifies','validates') and l.get('target_id')}, which is the direction master prompt section 13 declares: 'verifies: verification measure -> requirement/design'. Effect, measured on the corpus: the rule went from 12 false gaps to 0, and the validator's total finding count went from 21 to 9. The rule's intent is unchanged - a safety requirement with no verification at all is still reported - and the fix is STRICTLY HARDER to satisfy by accident than before, because a requirement appearing as the SOURCE of a verifies or validates link is a malformed link under the declared direction and no longer counts as verification of that requirement. Both directions are now proven by self-tests added to cmd_selftest: 'correctly directed verifies link (requirement as target) not flagged' passes, 'safety requirement with no verification link flagged' passes, and 'verifies link with requirement as source does not count as verification' passes. The self-test count went from 11 to 14, all passing. The same inversion was looked for in every other rule that reads a link endpoint and NOT found: the refines rule reads the FSR as the source and the safety goal as the target, which is the declared direction; the mitigates rule reads the safety goal as the source and the hazard as the target, which is the declared direction and matches the corpus's three mitigates links; the reviewed_by rule reads the target, which IS consistent with how the corpus stores reviewed_by links (review as source, artefact as target) - that storage is the reverse of the direction section 13 declares for the relation, which is a link-convention gap in the DATA and not a rule defect, is reported rather than fixed because correcting it would mean rewriting 167 links and is outside the scope of this finding, and does not cause any false finding today because the rule is consistent with the storage. No rule was weakened, relaxed or deleted, and no artifact was relabelled to dodge a rule. Findings FB2-REV-FND-000008..000012 and the seven fault_reaction findings remain OPEN: they are real conditions, and the finding's own point that authoring a measure is not verification evidence still stands. Human approval remains pending for every record named here: no human has confirmed this correction, no tool has been qualified, no certification is claimed and no ASPICE capability level is claimed. production_authorized stays false and product_verification_credit stays false on every record touched.
